title: Effects of 4-nonylphenol on oxidant/antioxidant balance system inducing hepatic steatosis in male rat.
ehr_evidence: Twenty-four male Sprague-Dawley rats (70–80 g) were obtained from the Experimental Animal Center of Tongji Medical College Animal Laboratory (Wuhan, China).
summary: Experimental study investigating the effects of intraperitoneal administration of 4-nonylphenol on hepatic steatosis, oxidative stress, and apoptosis in male rats.
key_findings: Liver weight significantly increased at 10 mg/kg (9.23 ± 0.78 g) and 50 mg/kg (9.44 ± 0.67 g) compared to control (7.63 ± 1.54 g).
Serum GOT, GPT, LDH, and γ-GT activities significantly increased in 4-NP-treated groups (p < 0.05 to p < 0.001).

H2O2 levels significantly increased at 50 mg/kg (3.066 ± 0.47 μmol/mg prot, p < 0.01) and MDA increased at 10 mg/kg (3.013 ± 0.46 nmol/mg prot, p < 0.01) and 50 mg/kg (3.199 ± 0.81 nmol/mg prot, p < 0.01).
Antioxidant enzymes CAT, GSH-Px, and SOD significantly decreased (p < 0.05 to p < 0.001).
Gene expression of Casp-9, Bax, Fas, FasL, and TNF-α significantly increased, while Bcl-2 significantly decreased (p < 0.05).
PCNA positive cells increased to 4.64%, 8.87%, and 9.07% at 2, 10, and 50 mg/kg doses respectively.
captured_features: Serum hepatic enzymes (GOT, GPT, LDH, γ-GT)
Gene expression (SOD1, GPx, HSP70, Casp-9, Bax, Bcl-2, Fas, FasL, TNF-α)
limitations: Intraperitoneal administration route may not reflect typical human environmental exposure
Lack of protein-level validation (immunoblotting recommended for future work)
Single species and strain limits generalizability
